tutorial.speaker: How to play
tutorial.text: Welcome, Scribe! This first level is your home. It's also where you'll learn how to play.

tutorial.speaker: How to play
tutorial.text: To walk, press and drag anywhere on the left side of the screen. A little joystick appears under your thumb. (On a keyboard, use WASD or the arrow keys.)

tutorial.speaker: How to play
tutorial.text: When you're close to someone or something, a gold button appears on the right. Tap it to talk, look or pick things up. (Keyboard: press E.)

tutorial.speaker: How to play
tutorial.text: Your current task is always at the top left, with a bar that fills up as you get closer to finishing it.

tutorial.speaker: How to play
tutorial.text: Gold gems float over people you still need to talk to, and sparkles mark things you can pick up. Bump into people and pets too. They'll have something to say!

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Tonight's the night. Dad says the time machine in the garage is finally ready.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Every Bible left in 2060 is a digital copy, and nobody can tell anymore which words have been changed.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: So I'm going back to the very beginning, to see it with my own eyes and write it down true, on real paper, where nobody can change it.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: First, I need to pack my satchel: a blank scroll, my reed pen, and the ink Dad mixed. Then I have to say goodbye to everyone.

tasks.go: Go to the time machine in the garage
tasks.explore_hint: Look around every room one last time.

items.name: Blank scroll
items.text: A blank scroll, rolled tight. By the time I come home, it'll hold the very first story ever written down.

items.name: Reed pen
items.text: My reed pen! Lily borrowed it for her drawings again. There's a tiny purple horse on the end of it now.

items.name: Bottle of ink
items.text: Dad's homemade ink: soot, gum and water, the way scribes made it thousands of years ago. Nobody can edit ink from far away.

packed.speaker: You
packed.text: Scroll, pen and ink. My satchel's packed.

family.name: Mom
family.question: What do you tell Mom?

talk.speaker: Mom
talk.text: There you are. I made your favorite tonight. I keep stirring the pot so I don't have to think about tomorrow.

talk.speaker: Mom
talk.text: Your room is going to be so quiet. I know you have to go. I just don't want to let go of you yet.

options: I'll miss you too, Mom. Every single day.
Someone has to write it down before it's lost forever.

replies.speaker: Mom
replies.text: Oh, sweetheart. Missing each other just means we love each other. That part never gets lost.

replies.speaker: Mom
replies.text: "The LORD watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another." I'll be praying that every night.

replies.speaker: Mom
replies.text: I know. Everyone else just complained that the words kept changing. You're the one who decided to do something about it.

replies.speaker: Mom
replies.text: "Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid... for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest."

after.speaker: Mom
after.text: I'm sad to see you go. But I have never been prouder of anyone in my whole life. Come here, my {child}.

again.speaker: Mom
again.text: Go on. We'll be right here when you get back. I'll keep your plate warm.

family.name: Dad
family.question: What do you tell Dad?

talk.speaker: Dad
talk.text: Hey, kiddo. Just tightening the last bolts. I've built that machine for two years, and now I almost wish it didn't work.

talk.speaker: Dad
talk.text: Every night I worked on it, I knew it was taking you somewhere I can't follow. Is this really what you want?

options: Yes. The truth is worth it, Dad.
You built it. Doesn't that mean you believe in this too?

replies.speaker: Dad
replies.text: Ha. You sound just like me when I was your age. Stubborn about the right things.

replies.speaker: Dad
replies.text: "And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free." Go and find it.

replies.speaker: Dad
replies.text: Yeah. I guess it does. I built it so that somebody could bring back what we lost.

replies.speaker: Dad
replies.text: I just didn't know that somebody would be my own kid.

after.speaker: Dad
after.text: I'm going to miss you something awful. But I'm so proud of you. You're brave enough to go and get the truth back for all of us.

after.speaker: Dad
after.text: Your ink's on the workbench, by the way. Don't leave without it.

again.speaker: Dad
again.text: Machine's warmed up and ready. Whenever you are.

bumps: Easy there, I'm holding a power cell.
Don't touch the blue wire. Trust me.

family.name: Sam
family.question: How do you explain it to Sam?

talk.speaker: Sam
talk.text: Mom says you're going back in time. Like, way back. Before dinosaurs back?

talk.speaker: Sam
talk.text: But why? The Bible's already on the tablet. I can just ask it to read me a story. Why do YOU have to go?

options: The tablet copies got changed, like someone scribbling in your favorite book.
Somebody has to see it for real and write it down so it never gets lost.

replies.speaker: Sam
replies.text: Someone scribbled in it? That's so mean! Like when I colored in your book, but on purpose?

replies.speaker: You
replies.text: Kind of like that. So nobody knows which parts are true anymore. I'm going to go see, and write it down right.

replies.speaker: Sam
replies.text: Okay... I think I get it. You're going to fix the book.

replies.speaker: Sam
replies.text: Like a real paper book? Nobody at my school has ever even seen one.

replies.speaker: You
replies.text: Exactly. Real ink on real paper. Then nobody can change it from far away, and you'll be able to read it yourself.

replies.speaker: Sam
replies.text: Whoa. Then I'll be the first kid with a real one.

after.speaker: You
after.text: I promise. Every story, in order, and then home.

after.speaker: Sam
after.text: Okay. Pinky promise counts double. You're the best {big} ever.

again.speaker: Sam
again.text: I'm building a time machine too. Out of blocks. It doesn't work yet.

bumps: Watch it, that's the moon base!

family.name: Lily
family.question: How do you explain it to Lily?

talk.speaker: Lily
talk.text: I'm drawing you a picture to take with you. It's you, in the time machine, and that's a horse. Probably.

talk.speaker: Lily
talk.text: But I don't get it. If the old stories are so important, why didn't anyone keep them? And why does it have to be you?

options: People trusted screens, and bad people changed the words over time.
Because I can't stop thinking about it. I think God wants me to go.

replies.speaker: Lily
replies.text: Changed them? Why would anybody do that?

replies.speaker: You
replies.text: Some people want the words to say what THEY want. A few people tried to save the old paper pages, but there are pieces missing.

replies.speaker: Lily
replies.text: So you're going to find the missing pieces. Like a puzzle.

replies.speaker: Lily
replies.text: Like when Samuel heard his name at night, and he said "Here am I"? Mom told me that one.

replies.speaker: You
replies.text: Kind of like that. And this time, I'm going to write it down so nobody forgets.

replies.speaker: Lily
replies.text: Okay. Then you'd better go. But you have to come back.

after.speaker: Lily
after.text: Here. Take my picture. Now you won't forget what we look like.

after.speaker: Lily
after.text: And I'm keeping your room clean. Mostly.

again.speaker: Lily
again.text: I'm adding Biscuit to the picture. He's the blob with ears.

looks.name: Your tablet
looks.note: Three digital copies of Genesis 1:1, and all three say something different. One has a whole verse missing. Which one is true? Nobody can say anymore.

looks.name: Your bed
looks.note: You won't sleep here for a long time. You smooth the quilt flat, just the way Mom likes it.

looks.name: Mirror
looks.note: You check the mirror. Traveling robe, sash, satchel. You look like a real scribe. A slightly nervous one.

looks.name: Bunk bed
looks.note: Sam sleeps on top so he can be "closer to space." Lily has six stuffed animals on hers, all lined up by size.

looks.name: Mirror
looks.note: Someone drew a smiley face in the steam on the mirror. You're pretty sure it was Sam.

looks.name: Wedding photo
looks.note: Mom and Dad on their wedding day, laughing at something. Dad still has that tie.

looks.name: Mirror
looks.note: Mom and Dad's bathroom. Dad's toothbrush is shaped like a rocket. It was a gift from Sam.

looks.name: Family bookshelf
looks.note: This shelf once held real paper books. Now it holds photos, and one empty spot Mom calls "saved for the Book."

looks.name: Holo-fireplace
looks.note: The fire isn't real, but it's warm. Every Christmas the whole family squeezes onto the sofa in front of it.

looks.name: Fridge
looks.note: Lily's drawing of the family is stuck to the fridge. You're the tall one holding a scroll.

looks.name: Holo-screen
looks.note: The news says another library archive was "updated" overnight. Nobody seems to know who did it, or what was changed.

looks.name: Board game
looks.note: A family game, half finished. Sam is winning. Sam is always winning.

looks.name: Hover car
looks.note: The family hover car. Dad says it's the second most important machine in the garage now.

looks.name: Engine block
looks.note: An old fusion engine on a stand, half taken apart. Dad pulled the main coil out of it for the time machine.

looks.name: Tool chest
looks.note: Every drawer is labeled in Dad's handwriting. The bottom one just says "MISC (DO NOT OPEN)."

looks.name: Old hover bike
looks.note: Dad's old hover bike. Half the time machine came from it, and the other half from late nights and a lot of prayer.

need_pack.speaker: You
need_pack.text: My satchel isn't packed. I still need: {items}.

need_talk.speaker: You
need_talk.text: And I haven't said goodbye to {people}. I'm not leaving without that.

need_talk_only.speaker: You
need_talk_only.text: I haven't said goodbye to {people} yet. I'm not leaving without that.

depart.speaker: Time machine
depart.text: Time machine online. Destination: In the beginning. Genesis, chapter 1.

depart.speaker: You
depart.text: Satchel. Scroll. Everyone I love, right here in my heart. Here we go.

send_off.speaker: Dad
send_off.text: Hands inside the ring, kiddo. We love you.

send_off.speaker: Mom
send_off.text: We're so proud of you! Be careful!
